_doc: doc 03 §2.5b — THE COMMISSIONS BOARD. Work the city takes on a clock, run by `sim/economy/contract_board.gd` on the `contracts` RNG stream. This file owns WHICH commissions exist, WHAT each one asks the player to do, HOW LONG they run and WHEN the board is allowed to post one. **It owns no dollar** (C-07, report 98 §60 RR-170): every payout is priced by `data/economy.json`'s `city_services.contract_payout`, the same split RR-78 gave doc 06's dispatch rewards and RR-85 gave doc 06 §2.16's street bounties. `ContractBoard.FORBIDDEN_KEYS` refuses a price put back, at any depth, as a BOOT ERROR.
_why: The 2026-09-03 overnight report asked for two things this file exists for: a single collection worth about $15,000, and 'any other fun ideas to collect money in the game, something to actually DO to collect, other than tax revenue'. The first cannot be answered on the street layer — 15,000 at that layer's measured 0.339 offers/gh is $5,090/gh, 1.85x the whole net income of a level-6 city — so the number belongs to a verb that fires about once a game-day, and this is it.
_offline: doc 08 §2.3 rule 9 — the board does NOT run while the player is away. `advance(dt, online=false)` returns before its first statement: no offer is posted, no deadline runs down, no offer ages out, and the `contracts` stream is not advanced by a single call. A player who closes the app mid-commission finds it with exactly the hours they left it with. That also means the balance matrix, which runs the coarse step, cannot see this file at all.
_kinds: Every `kind` below is a row in `GoalSystem.EVENT_KINDS` or in `ContractBoard.EXTRA_EVENT_KINDS`, which is one row — `restore_buildings`, whose event did not exist until Wave 18 gave the restore a verb. The board invents NO objective vocabulary: a commission can only ask for something doc 09's curriculum already knows how to notice, so a verb that grows a curriculum objective grows a contract kind for free, and a kind named here that no evaluator knows is DROPPED at parse with a boot error rather than silently sitting at zero progress forever.
_verbs: Every row is answerable with a door that exists today: `lay_streets` through the build sheet's ROADS tab and the drag-path tool, `patrol` through the street layer's tap (doc 06 §2.16), `retainer` through the incident drawer's auto and manual dispatch both, `assessor` through the building panel's REPAIR, `insurance`/`reconstruction` through the building panel's RESTORE (Wave 18), `convention` through the building panel's UPGRADE. `tests/test_contracts.gd` holds this file to the reachable set the same way `tests/test_goals_system.gd` holds data/goals.json to it.
_level_gate: `min_city_level` is a BALANCE gate and not a difficulty curve. `data/economy.json pacing_guardrails.MODEL_NET_PER_HOUR_BY_CITY_LEVEL` is flat from level 2 to level 5 and then TRIPLES, so a `major` payout only fits inside `CONTRACT_CEILING_SHARE_MAX` at the top rung and is refused below it. See doc 92 §57.3.

board._note: `offer_interval_h` is the mean game-hours between posting attempts that clear the Bernoulli, evaluated once per game-hour (the phase adapter's own cadence, never authored here). One game-hour is one real minute at 1x, so 6.0 is 'something new appears on the board every few minutes while there is room for it'.
board._cooldown_note: THE INCOME BOUND, and it is the only one. The city holds exactly one commission at a time, so the fastest a player can earn from this layer is one payout per (time to finish + this cooldown). 30.0 is fitted against `CONTRACT_CEILING_SHARE_MAX` 0.25 at every rung of the level ladder — see doc 92 §57.3's table. It suppresses OFFERS as well as accepts, so the quiet stretch after a delivery is visible on the board rather than only in a refusal.

templates._note: The neighbourhood watch pays per pickup. It is the tutorial contract of this layer: the work is the tap the player already knows, the deadline is short, and it teaches that a commission is accepted BEFORE the work counts.

A film unit wants fresh tarmac for a chase scene. Counts road TILES stamped, so a single drag can finish it — which is the point: it is the commission that rewards a player for doing a thing they were going to do anyway, and teaches that the board is worth reading before you build.

The insurer pays for stock brought back, and it is the row the 2026-09-03 report is about: a player restoring a flooded city is doing this work anyway and was being paid nothing for it. Level 2 rather than 1 because a founding city has nothing destroyed yet and an unfinishable commission on the board is worse than an empty one.

The county pays a retainer for incidents answered. Counts resolutions of any type, auto or manual, so it rewards a city that RESPONDS rather than one that happens to have the right station — and it is the one commission a player can finish by working the drawer.

A condition survey the city is paid to pass. Counts repairs STARTED, which is doc 02 §2.6's verb and the one the Wave-18 Upkeep band already teaches; the fiction is that the assessor pays for the work order, not for the crew's arrival.

The convention bureau needs capacity, and capacity is doc 02's ladder rather than doc 02's roster — it counts UPGRADES, not new builds, which is the lesson level 2 of the curriculum teaches and the one a rich player stops practising.

A state reconstruction grant, and the biggest single thing a player can collect in this game. It pays at least $15,000 at level 6 — the player's own number, on the verb they were already using at three in the morning: 'I've been trying to restore all the buildings so we can get revenue back up.'

_no_penalty: RULED, v1 (doc 93 §AQ3). A contract that runs out of hours costs the player NOTHING — no fee, no stability ding, no reputation. The layer exists because a playtester asked for something to DO, and a penalty for not finishing converts an opportunity into a chore; it would also tax precisely the player who put the phone down, which is the player doc 08 §2.3 rule 9 promises not to punish. It is the same ruling `data/street.json`'s `expire_stability_delta: 0.0` makes for an unanswered crook, and it re-opens on the same one condition: telemetry showing players farm-ignoring commissions at scale.
_tests: tests/test_contracts.gd — the offer/accept/progress/claim lifecycle, the coarse contract (zero draws, zero aging, zero offers while away), a save->load round-trip mid-contract, the level gate, the price guard (this file carries no dollar at any depth and a tier the economy does not price is a boot error), and that progress counts only against an ACCEPTED contract.
